points.description: States that the star (*) operator returns an alias (synonym) for the object/the name of the object that its operand points to in memory (i.e., the object at the address the pointer holds), stated precisely.
points.partial_credit: Half: says it returns the object/value the operand points to but does not mention alias/synonym for the object.

points.description: Names the operator correctly as the dereferencing (indirection) operator.
Correctly distinguishes it from the address-of operator (&) / from returning the pointer or address itself: the operand is a pointer and the result is the pointed-to object, not the address.
points.partial_credit: Half: states operand is a pointer/address and result is the object, without explicit contrast with the address or &.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise fact: * returns an alias for the object its operand (a pointer) points to, and it is called the dereferencing operator. Vague wording such as "returns a value" or "something in memory" earns nothing on P1. Any wrong statement, such as saying it returns the address, loses the affected point.
